messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph on rural interstates).
• In cities: 25–45 mph; 35 mph in school zones during school hours.
• “No Speed Limit” signs allow drivers to set a safe speed. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001‑545.004 | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children 5–7 years old. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit: 0.08% for adults, 0.02% for commercial drivers.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (any detectable BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, jail time, and ignition interlock devices. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.051‑545.055 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Handheld phone use is prohibited while driving (except for emergency calls).
• “Hands‑free” devices are allowed but driver must remain attentive. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.041 | | **Right‑of‑Way & Yield Rules** | • Stop at stop signs, yield at yield signs, and give right‑of‑way to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles approaching from the right. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.011‑545.015 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children.
• No passing on either side of a stopped bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.025 | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep within lane markings; avoid weaving.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.013 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces without proper permit, or in front of driveways.
• Parking meters and municipal regulations apply in cities. | Local ordinances + Texas Transportation Code § 545.019 | | **Vehicle Safety Standards** | • Must have valid registration, insurance, and a current inspection sticker.
• Vehicle must pass annual safety inspections in most counties. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.006 | | **Special Situations** | • School zone speed limits: 25 mph (or 20 mph in some districts) during school hours.
• Construction zones: posted signs may lower speed limits temporarily. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.014 | ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Official site for registration, licensing, and law updates. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text available online via the Texas Legislature’s website. 3. **Local County Courts** – For recent case law and enforcement trends. 4. **Legal Aid Organizations** – Offer guidance on specific cases (e.g., DUI defense, traffic ticket disputes). --- #### Quick Reference Links - TxDMV Traffic Law Overview: https://www.txdmv.gov/traffic-laws - Texas Transportation Code (PDF): https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TN/htm/TN.545.htm - Texas Court Cases Database (search by keyword): https://www.courtlistener.com/?q=Texas+traffic+laws Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed information on a specific area—such as DUI penalties, school zone rules, or how to appeal a traffic ticket!
